decision.reason: The incumbent is a public type dependency and a byte-format dependency across HTTP, gRPC, two persisted ATP envelopes, manifest size metadata, and OTLP; a public but unwired ATP transform also exposes it. The current HTTP deflate token emits raw RFC 1951 rather than an RFC 1950 zlib envelope, production payload distributions are unavailable, cross-implementation service evidence is blocked, persisted decoders have unresolved allocation and envelope-boundary gaps, and the browser target cell was unavailable. Replacing the backend before those gaps close would guess at observable compatibility.

dependency_resolution.marginal_graph_boundary: crc32fast is a direct runtime dependency and is not removable with flate2. miniz_oxide is also reachable through the optional backtrace package in the lockfile, so this list is a compression-profile delta, not a whole-workspace package-removal claim.

surface_inventory.streaming: State persists across repeated chunk calls. Encoder finish finalizes once; decoder calls flush per input chunk and finish finalizes the stream.
surface_inventory.limits: Compressed output accepts Option<usize>; middleware defaults to 16 MiB. Gzip decompression requires a DecompressionLimit, whose default is 16 MiB; raw-deflate decompression still accepts Option<usize>. Limits are enforced before LimitedWriter grows.

formats: one RFC 1952 gzip member per compressed gRPC message
surface_inventory.streaming: One-shot per message; codec state is not shared across messages.
surface_inventory.limits: Both the on-wire frame and inflated message are bounded by the configured decode limit; the default is 4 MiB.

formats: one RFC 1952 gzip member plus first-party size descriptor
surface_inventory.limits: Default minimum input 1024 bytes, minimum saving 64 bytes and 500 basis points. Restore checks encoded size, declared original size, caller cap, actual produced size, and overflow.

formats: ASUPCACHE\u0000 version 1 codec 1 containing one RFC 1952 gzip member
surface_inventory.limits: Only content above 1024 bytes is attempted; level 6; compressed bytes plus 60-byte envelope must be smaller. Envelope pins original length, encoded length, and SHA-256 plaintext digest. Decode currently trusts the declared original length for Vec capacity and has no caller cap.
downstream_consumers: ATP file cache users and existing cache files

formats: ASUPMBX1 version 1 compressed flag containing one RFC 1952 gzip member
surface_inventory.limits: Default chunk size 1 MiB; content above 1024 bytes is attempted at level 6 and retained only when smaller. Decode checks declared original size against configured chunk size and verifies stored lengths and plaintext digest, but read_to_end can grow beyond the declared size before the final equality check.
downstream_consumers: ATP mailbox users and existing mailbox chunks

surface_inventory.streaming: One-shot size calculation; compressed bytes are not persisted here.
surface_inventory.limits: Policy threshold and object-kind filter apply; configured level is capped at 9 for the size calculation.

formats: one RFC 1952 gzip member per OTLP HTTP request
surface_inventory.limits: Compression defaults off. Requesting it without the feature returns an explicit error rather than downgrading.
downstream_consumers: OTLP metrics, traces, and logs exporters

formats: one RFC 1952 gzip member over deterministic JSON

surface_inventory.limits: No module declaration reaches this directory; it is neither implementation nor coverage.

surface_inventory.streaming: No encoder, decoder, context-takeover state, window-bit parser, or RFC 7692 tail handling exists.

formats: Kafka gzip record batches owned by librdkafka
surface_inventory.streaming: Owned by librdkafka rather than an asupersync codec.
surface_inventory.limits: No local member, flush, dictionary, or decoder semantics are exposed by the Rust implementation.

gzip.producer_members: exactly one member per HTTP stream, gRPC message, ATP object/chunk, persisted payload, or OTLP request
gzip.decoder_scope: HTTP explicitly rejects concatenated members. Other read-adapter callers are single-member consumers but do not all prove rejection of trailing or concatenated data.
gzip.default_header: GzEncoder::new emits the locked flate2 default 10-byte header with no optional fields, MTIME 0 and OS 255.

raw_deflate.producer_scope: HTTP Content-Encoding deflate and non-production reference harness
raw_deflate.compatibility_rule: The shipped raw bytes are frozen for inventory purposes even though HTTP deflate is normally defined as a zlib-wrapped stream.

zlib_wrapper.compatibility_gap: The ContentEncoding documentation says wrapped in zlib, but the implementation and vectors use raw DeflateEncoder and DeflateDecoder.

flush_and_finish.http_gzip_compress: write chunks without forcing a sync flush; finish flushes and finalizes once
flush_and_finish.http_deflate_compress: write chunks without forcing a sync flush; finish finalizes once
flush_and_finish.http_gzip_decompress: write and flush each input chunk; finish validates and finalizes
flush_and_finish.http_deflate_decompress: write and flush each input chunk; finish validates and finalizes
flush_and_finish.one_shot_callers: write_all plus finish, or read until EOF

feature_off.http: encoding vocabulary and negotiation remain; factories return None for real codecs and identity remains available
feature_off.atp_cache: configured compression above threshold returns an error
feature_off.atp_mailbox: stored compressed chunks cannot be decoded
feature_off.otlp: requesting compression returns an explicit error

gaps.summary: HTTP deflate emits raw RFC 1951 while documentation describes an RFC 1950 zlib wrapper.
No current zlib-wrapper or preset-dictionary surface exists, so any future support decision needs explicit compatibility authority.
The capability registry omits live ATP transport, cache, mailbox, manifest, and OTLP owners.
The capability registry says planned while the capability baseline says executable complete.
The named real-service compression scenario is not registered.
No production payload distribution or compression performance receipt exists.
The browser target was unavailable and Apple and Windows cells were not run.
Remote cargo tree evidence is unavailable because RCH refuses non-compilation commands and local fallback is prohibited.
Only the HTTP decoder has an explicit concatenated-member rejection contract; other single-member consumers lack a uniform trailing-data contract.
Four public constructors expose flate2::Compression directly.
The public ATP transport transform has no production TCP, RQ, or QUIC caller, so its bytes are not live transport evidence.
Raw cache content beginning with ASUPCACHE followed by a NUL byte is interpreted as an envelope because the raw fallback has no escaping rule.
Cache decode allocates from the envelope-declared original size without a configured upper bound.
Mailbox decode checks the declared size against chunk_size but read_to_end can allocate beyond it before the final exact-size rejection.
WebSocket can negotiate the permessage-deflate token without implementing the RFC 7692 transform.
gRPC classifies literal deflate and snappy encodings as compressed in one decode path while the production codec registry wires only identity and gzip.
The real-http compression files are undeclared test source and contain stale or simulated transforms, so they are not executable interoperability evidence.

required_parity_scope: Preserve the optional compression feature and feature-off behavior for every live caller.

Preserve public gzip and deflate streaming types, factory behavior, output limits, error poisoning, idempotent finish, and the four flate2::Compression constructor signatures unless a separately approved breaking API change is made.
Preserve gzip RFC 1952 bytes and single-member production boundaries across HTTP, gRPC, ATP transport, cache, mailbox, manifest size calculation, and OTLP.
Preserve the current raw RFC 1951 HTTP deflate bytes until the raw-versus-zlib discrepancy is separately adjudicated with interoperability evidence.
Preserve ASUPCACHE version 1 codec 1 and ASUPMBX1 version 1 compressed-flag decoding for existing persisted data.
Preserve gRPC compressed-flag framing, the default 4 MiB directional limits, and per-message codec reset.
Preserve HTTP negotiation, x-gzip alias, server preference, 16 MiB compressed-output default, sensitivity policy, header rewriting, and identity fallback.
Preserve ATP thresholds, descriptors, exact length checks, digest checks, and fail-closed feature-off behavior.
Decide whether the public but unwired ATP transform is retained and wire it only with its own transport and persisted-format evidence.
Bound cache and mailbox decode allocation before treating either persisted envelope as replacement-ready, and preserve raw cache values that collide with the envelope magic.
Preserve OTLP compression default-off and explicit feature-missing error.
Keep Kafka gzip scoped to its external backend and do not count WebSocket permessage-deflate advertisement as an implemented codec.
Do not infer Brotli parity from any DEFLATE result.
